descriptionChirho: To deliver or rescue someone from danger, enemies, or distress, used in the Piel stem as a causative action of setting free.
The Piel participle used as a substantive noun meaning 'deliverer, rescuer,' typically as a divine epithet for God.
To escape or get away from danger, used intransitively in the Qal stem or reflexively in the Piel cohortative.
To carry off or snatch away, used in the Hifil stem with the sense of removing or taking away forcibly.
To bring forth or deliver a child, a specialized physical sense of causing to come out, distinct from rescue.
